questions.enonce_markdown:
Define the following:

(i) Immigration.

(ii) Population census.

(iii) Death rate.

(iv) Rural exodus.

(2+2+2+2=8 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Immigration** is the movement of people **into** a country from another country in order to settle there, either permanently or for a long period (for example, a Nigerian trader who comes to settle and work in Douala).

**(ii) Population census** is the official counting of all the people living in a country at a given time, together with the collection of information about them (age, sex, occupation, education, place of residence). It is usually repeated at regular intervals.

**(iii) Death rate** (crude death rate) is the number of deaths per 1,000 people of the population in a country in one year.

**(iv) Rural exodus** (rural-urban migration) is the large movement of people, mostly young people, from villages and rural areas to towns and cities, in search of jobs, better wages, schools, hospitals and other amenities.

questions.enonce_markdown:
State and explain **Four (04)** effects of rural urban migration to the urban centres.

(8 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** *Rural-urban migration* is the movement of people from the countryside to towns and cities. It has the following effects on the urban centres.

1. **Overcrowding and housing shortage.** The number of people in towns grows faster than the number of houses, so rents rise, many people live in slums or in poor, crowded housing and unplanned neighbourhoods grow on the edge of the city.
2. **Unemployment and underemployment.** The migrants arrive in greater numbers than the jobs available in the towns, so many become unemployed or work in the informal sector (hawking, motor-bike taxi, small trading) with low and irregular incomes.
3. **Increase in crime and social problems.** Jobless young people may turn to theft, begging, drug abuse and prostitution, so the police and the courts must deal with more insecurity.
4. **Pressure on social amenities and public services.** More people share the same water, electricity, roads, schools, hospitals and transport, causing water and power cuts, traffic jams, long queues and poor sanitation and pollution.
5. **Larger labour supply and bigger market (a positive effect).** Industries and building firms find cheap and abundant labour and the larger population increases the demand for goods and services, which can encourage the growth of industries and trade in the towns.

*Any four of these effects, each stated and explained, earn full marks.*

**Conclusion.** Rural-urban migration brings some benefits (labour and markets) to the towns, but if it is not controlled it leads mainly to congestion, unemployment, insecurity and heavy pressure on public services.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Distinguish between a growing population and an ageing population.

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **growing population** is one whose **total size is increasing** from year to year, because the birth rate is higher than the death rate (natural increase), sometimes helped by immigration. It usually has a large proportion of young people and children, so the base of its age pyramid is wide (the case in many developing countries).

An **ageing population** is one in which the **proportion of old people** (for example those aged 65 and above) in the total population is **rising**, because the birth rate falls and life expectancy rises, so there are relatively fewer young people. Its age pyramid is narrow at the base and wide at the top; the burden of pensions and health care for the old increases while the labour force becomes smaller.

**Distinction:** the first concerns the *size* of the population (more people in total), the second concerns its *age structure* (more old people in proportion). A population can grow and age at the same time.
